Well, my supervisor said I needed to come down here because... well, my talking gets all mixed up lately. Like, I'll just be trying to explain something simple about the keys. The heavy brass ones for the service elevator, you know? I keep them on a big ring. But then the way they jingle, it makes me think about the jail. My cousin was in the county jail for a bit back in the nineties, and they have those heavy doors... 

Anyway, I try to tell people about the jail, and then the prayer rug. I found this real nice prayer rug while I was mopping the third floor hallway last week. Just sitting there. And the chess pieces, too! Someone left all these glass chess pieces right next to the utility closet. I try to explain to everybody how it all goes together, the keys and the jail and the rug and the little glass horses, but... people just get frustrated with me. They tell me they cannot follow what I am saying. So I guess that's what brings me in. My words just get all scrambled up and nobody can follow me.

Well, yeah, it's real. I mean, it sounds just as real as you sitting right there. Sometimes I'll just be in the mop closet, you know, getting the bucket ready, or walking past the air vents, and there it is. A man's voice. He says my name, or he tells me I ruined everything.

My buddy Dale, the one with the Ford pickup, he used to put in these cassette tapes of old country music. Those pliers were rusty, too, because he left them in the bed of the truck and it rained for three days straight.

Yeah, it... it really messes things up for me. I've missed shifts at the school, and I actually lost some extra cleaning work I used to do on the side because of it. Leaves are such a pain in the fall, especially oak leaves. They don't break down like maple leaves do; they just sit there on the lawn getting all leathery and tough. Discos were huge when I was a teenager, with the mirror balls and the polyester suits... but yeah, I can't really get my work done or be around people because I just don't make sense to them.

Well, I try to have clear times, but that's actually what brings me here, I guess. My talking just gets all mixed up. Like, I'll try to explain to someone about my keys, you know, the big heavy ring of keys I use at the school. I try to explain to everybody how it all goes together, the keys and the jail and the rug and the little glass horses, but... people just get frustrated with me. They tell me they cannot follow what I am saying. So I guess that's what brings me in. My words just get all scrambled up and nobody can follow me.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like your thoughts are connected in a way that makes sense to you, even if others have trouble following?\n\nPatient: Well, yeah, to me it makes perfect sense. That's what I was just saying, you know? My talking gets all mixed up for them, but in my head, it's a straight line. I try to explain about the keys, and then the jail, and the prayer rug, and those little glass chess pieces... and to me, they all fit together. \n\nBecause the glass horses, they catch the light from the fluorescent tubes in the ceiling. Those tubes buzz real loud on the third floor. It's a low hum, kind of like... kind of like the engine on this old Ford pickup my buddy Dale had back in '88. We drove that truck all the way down to Pensacola. Dale, he was always talking about buying a boat and going deep-sea fishing. I never liked the ocean much myself, the salt makes my skin itch real bad. I had to use this special lotion for a month once just to get it to stop peeling. \n\nBut... anyway, what was I... oh, right. People at work. Like I told you, they just tell me they cannot follow what I am saying. It's like I'm speaking a different language, but I'm just trying to show them how the rug and the keys go together.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever hear or see things that other people do not?\n\nPatient: Well, yeah, sometimes I do. Like... I'll be working, right? Just doing my rounds. And I'll hear this man's voice. It comes right out of the air vents, or sometimes when I'm in the mop closet mixing the floor cleaner. He says my name, or he tells me I ruined everything. And I'm telling you, it sounds just as real as you sitting right there. \n\nIt's like how my old landlord, Mr. Henderson, used to yell at me through the screen door. He had this screen door where the mesh was all rusted out at the bottom because his dog, Buster, kept scratching at it. Buster was a beagle mix, I think. Howled all night whenever the sirens went past on 4th Street. The fire station was right down the block, you see, so they'd go by a lot. \n\nAnyway, the fire trucks used to be this bright, cherry red, but now they paint them that weird yellow-green color. They say it's easier to see at night, which I guess makes sense. Nighttime is when the streetlights buzz the loudest. Kind of like the fluorescent tubes I was telling you about... but yeah, the voice. It just tells me I ruined it all.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is real?\n\nPatient: Well, yeah, it's real. I mean, it sounds just as real as you sitting right there. Sometimes I'll just be in the mop closet, you know, getting the bucket ready, or walking past the air vents, and there it is. A man's voice. He says my name, or he tells me I ruined everything. \n\nIt's just like... well, it's like when you hear the radio playing from someone's car when they drive by with the windows down. My buddy Dale, the one with the Ford pickup, he used to put in these cassette tapes of old country music. He had this one tape, I think it was George Jones, and the tape got all chewed up in the player once. We had to pull it out with a pair of needle-nose pliers. Those pliers were rusty, too, because he left them in the bed of the truck and it rained for three days straight. \n\nIt rained so hard that year, the creek behind my aunt's house flooded right up to the back porch. She had these nice wicker chairs out there, and they got completely ruined. The water just soaked right into the wood. Wood is funny like that, it absorbs everything. Kind of like a sponge. Sponges are what I use when I have to scrub the baseboards on the second floor. They get so scuffed up from people's shoes. But yeah... the voice, it sounds completely real to me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is talking to you alone or can others hear it too?\n\nPatient: Well, I think... I think it's just for me. Because nobody else is ever around when it happens, you know? Like I said, it's just me in the mop closet, or walking by the vents, and I hear this man's voice saying my name or telling me I ruined everything. It sounds exactly like someone standing right next to me, but... but there's nobody there. \n\nIt's kind of like how nobody else used to hear the stray cats fighting under the porch at my old place. I lived in this duplex over on Elm Street, and the landlord never fixed the skirting. So these cats would get under there and just yowl all night long. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she was half deaf anyway, so she never heard a thing. She used to bake these incredible peach cobblers, though. She'd bring me a slice every Sunday on this little blue plate with a chip on the edge. \n\nI always wondered how that plate got chipped. Maybe she dropped it in the sink. Sinks get so grimy if you don't use the right kind of abrasive cleaner. You gotta use the powder kind, not the liquid, if you really want to get the stains out. The liquid just kind of slides right off the porcelain. Porcelain is a lot like glass, I guess... like those chess pieces I was talking about. But, yeah, nobody else seems to hear the man's voice. Just me.\n\nDoctor: When you're thinking about all these things like the keys, the jail, and the prayer rug, do you feel like you can control how your thoughts jump from one thing to another?\n\nPatient: No, I... I can't really control it. That's actually what brings me here, you know? My talking just gets all mixed up. I'll be trying to explain something, like the keys, and then suddenly I'm talking about the jail, and then the prayer rug, and then those glass chess pieces... and people just look at me like I'm crazy. They tell me they cannot follow what I am saying at all. \n\nIt's frustrating, because in my head it all connects, like a string of Christmas lights. You know how when one bulb goes out on those old cheap strands, the whole line goes dark? I used to hang those lights up around the gutters every November. Had this aluminum ladder that was always a little wobbly on the left side. I think one of the rubber feet fell off when I was moving out of that duplex on Elm Street. \n\nMoving is such a hassle. You end up finding all this stuff you forgot you even owned. Like I found this old box of matchbooks I used to collect from diners. There was this one diner out on Route 9 that made the best meatloaf sandwich. You can boil 'em, mash 'em, fry 'em... but yeah, my thoughts just kind of go on their own trip, and people can't keep up with me.\n\nDoctor: Do you have times when your thoughts are clear and you can explain things without getting mixed up?\n\nPatient: Well, no, not really. I mean, that's the whole reason I'm sitting here talking to you right now. Like I was saying before, what brings me here is my talking just gets all mixed up. I'll be trying to explain something simple, like the keys, and then before I know it I'm talking about the jail, and then that prayer rug, and then those glass chess pieces. And people just stare at me. They tell me they cannot follow what I am saying at all. \n\nIt's like... it's like when you try to follow a recipe but you lose your place in the cookbook. My mom had this old Betty Crocker cookbook, the one with the red and white checkered cover. The spine was completely held together with duct tape. Duct tape is amazing stuff, really. I use it all the time at work. Just last week, one of the vacuum cleaner hoses got a crack in it, right near the handle, and I just wrapped it up with duct tape. \n\nThose vacuums are so heavy, though. They're the industrial kind, the ones you strap on your back like a backpack. It really does a number on your shoulders if you wear it too long. I have to stretch out my arms every night or I wake up stiff as a board. Boards... like the floorboards in the gymnasium. They need to be refinished every summer. The varnish smells so strong it gives you a headache if you don't open the double doors. But yeah, my talking just... it just gets mixed up, and people can't understand me.\n\nDoctor: Do you find it difficult to complete tasks at work or at home because your thoughts are disorganized?\n\nPatient: Yeah, it... it really messes things up for me. I've missed shifts at the school, and I actually lost some extra cleaning work I used to do on the side because of it. People just tell me they can't rely on me anymore, or they can't understand what I'm trying to say. I even stopped going to the mosque for prayers, and I don't go to family gatherings either. It's just too hard when everyone's looking at you like you're speaking a different language. \n\nLanguages are fascinating, though. My uncle used to speak a little bit of French he picked up when he was stationed overseas. He brought back this beautiful brass compass from his time in the service. It had these intricate engravings all around the edge, like little vines and leaves. Leaves are such a pain in the fall, especially oak leaves. They don't break down like maple leaves do; they just sit there on the lawn getting all leathery and tough. You really need a good mulching mower to deal with them. \n\nI used to have a Toro mower, the self-propelled kind. It was red, bright red, like a fire engine. Fire engines are so loud when they go by, but I guess they have to be. Actually, there were a few times things got so bad with my head and my talking that people had to call for emergency help because they said I wasn't safe. The paramedics came in one of those big trucks with the flashing lights. The lights reflect off the windows of the houses at night, making everything look like a disco. Discos were huge when I was a teenager, with the mirror balls and the polyester suits... but yeah, I can't really get my work done or be around people because I just don't make sense to them.\n\nDoctor: Do you often find yourself doing things in a way that seems unusual or inappropriate to others?\n\nPatient: Well, I don't... I don't really know what you mean by unusual. I just do things the way I do them, you know? But people are always watching. Like fake oranges and pumice stone. It's gritty. Gritty like the sand at the beach... I haven't been to the beach in years. The paneling was peeling off near the back tire. Tires are so expensive now. You go to get a new set and it's like a whole week's paycheck. And then they try to sell you on the alignment and the balancing... but yeah, I don't really have times where it's totally clear. It's mostly just like this.\n\nDoctor: Do you have any periods where your thoughts are completely clear and organized, without any mixing up?\n\nPatient: Well, I try to have clear times, but that's actually what brings me here, I guess. Well, no, it wasn't always like this. I mean, I used to be able to tell a story straight through, you know? But it's been... I'd say about two years and five months now. It started right after that brief detention I had, over that misunderstanding at the building where I work.

They bake them in kilns, these massive ovens. I always wondered how hot a kiln has to get to turn clay into a rock basically. Clay is so soft. When I was in school, before I dropped out, we had an art class where we made these little pinch pots out of clay. Mine was terrible, it was all lopsided. The teacher, Mrs. Gable, she had these huge thick glasses that magnified her eyes so they looked like giant marbles. Marbles used to be a huge game, kids would play them in the dirt. You'd have your shooter marble, the big heavy one. Glass can be so beautiful, especially sea glass. When you find it on the beach, it's all frosted and smooth from the waves tumbling it around for years and years... 

But yeah, it's been about two years and five months since the detention thing, that's when my talking started getting all tangled up.

I... I mean, I don't know if it ever completely stops. That's the whole reason I'm here, really. My talking just gets all mixed up. Like, I'll be trying to explain something simple, you know?
